title: Did You Give Your Brain a Workout Today
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece treats sustained concentration as a genuine physical workout for the brain, citing figures on the calories burned through everyday thinking and conversation compared to focused deep work. Drawing on Cal Newport's concept of Deep Work, the author argues that maintaining unbroken focus over longer stretches of time can roughly double the brain's typical caloric burn. The piece frames the discipline required to sustain deep focus as directly analogous to physical exercise: it takes intention and consistency to build, and it atrophies quickly without practice. The takeaway for leaders is that mental and physical conditioning reinforce each other, and neither substitutes for the other.
points: The brain burns meaningful energy during difficult intellectual tasks, not just physical exertion.
Sustained, unbroken focus -- what Cal Newport calls Deep Work -- can roughly double typical mental calorie burn.
Deep focus requires the same intention and consistency as physical exercise, and fades just as quickly without practice.
Physical and mental conditioning reinforce one another; leadership strength depends on both.
quotes: Moderate physical exertion, such as weightlifting, bicycling, and rowing, burns about 6 calories per minute on average, while engaging in difficult intellectual tasks, such as working through a complex decision or playing chess, burns roughly 2 calories per minute.
Even though the adult human brain is only 2 percent of total body weight, it demands 20 percent of resting metabolic rate.
Developing the discipline to do deep work is no different than creating habits that help us hop on an exercise bike each day.
Great leaders stay in shape both physically and mentally. The best news is that the two arenas feed one another when done consistently and with vigor.
Getting in tip-top shape requires both physical and mental exercise.
Leaders who work hard to get themselves in great shape invest time to challenge themselves physically and intellectually each and every day.
On a typical day, leaders burn through about 320 calories just by thinking and conversing with others.
Unfortunately, the brain has a hard time staying focused on just one thing for too long.
